english: Is it okay to talk (on the phone) right now?
usage: Is now a good time to talk?
polite opener when YOU called someone
Are you free to talk right now?
지금 = right now, makes timing explicit
Do you have a minute to talk?
examples: 여보세요, 김 대리님? 지금 통화 괜찮으세요?
Hello, is this Mr. Kim? Is now a good time to talk?
standard business call opener
바쁘신데 죄송해요. 잠깐 통화 괜찮으세요?
Sorry to bother you when you're busy. Do you have a minute?
apologetic, very polite
야, 지금 통화 괜찮아? 할 말 있어.
Hey, can you talk now? I've got something to say.
반말, between close friends
nuance: The default phone courtesy line right after the other person picks up — you check whether they can actually talk before launching in. 괜찮으세요? is the safe polite form for anyone you'd use 존댓말 with; drop to 괜찮아? only with close friends. Koreans use this constantly, so saying it makes you sound considerate rather than abrupt.
mistakes: Saying it when YOU received the call — the caller asks this, not the person who answered.
Using 괜찮아? with a boss or client; it sounds too familiar — use 괜찮으세요?.

english: Please hold (don't hang up), and wait a moment
usage: Please don't hang up and hold on
full polite form, said to a caller
Please stay on the line for a moment
examples: 담당자 확인해 드릴게요. 끊지 말고 기다려 주세요.
I'll check with the person in charge. Please hold.
service/call-center line
끊지 마시고 잠시만 기다려 주세요. 바로 연결해 드리겠습니다.
Please hold a moment; I'll connect you right away.
formal customer service
엄마한테 물어볼게. 끊지 말고 기다려.
I'll ask Mom. Don't hang up, hold on.
casual, to a friend
nuance: What an agent or whoever answered says when they need to step away briefly but want you to stay on the line. 끊다 literally means 'to cut/sever,' which is how Korean expresses hanging up. The -지 말고 ('don't ~ and') warns against hanging up while 기다려 주세요 asks you to wait — together it's the standard 'please hold.'
mistakes: Confusing 끊다 (hang up) with 끄다 (turn off) — phones get 끊어, devices get 꺼.
Dropping 주세요 and just saying 끊지 말고 기다려 to a customer — sounds like an order.

english: Shall I take a message (for them)?
usage: Would you like me to leave a message?
offering to relay a message — humble
Is there a message you'd like to leave?
Want me to leave them a message?
examples: 지금 자리에 안 계세요. 메모 남겨 드릴까요?
They're not at their desk right now. Shall I take a message?
classic office phone answer
회의 중이신데, 메모 남겨 드릴까요?
They're in a meeting — would you like to leave a message?
polite, common at work
형 지금 없는데, 메모 남겨 줄까?
Bro's not here — want me to pass on a message?
casual, at home
nuance: Said by whoever answers when the person you want is unavailable, offering to write down a message. 드리다 is the humble verb for 'give/do for someone,' so 남겨 드릴까요? politely offers to do the favor of taking a note for the absent party. This is the natural service-register way to handle a missed connection.
mistakes: Using 남겨 줄까요? to a customer — 드릴까요? is more appropriately humble.
Writing 남기다 as 남끼다; the verb stem is 남기- (남겨 = 남기 + 어).

usage: I'll connect you to the right department
반말 / passing the phone to someone
examples: 기술 지원팀으로 연결해 드릴게요. 잠시만요.
I'll connect you to tech support. One moment.
call-center transfer
제가 처리할 수 없는 건이라, 담당자에게 연결해 드릴게요.
This isn't something I can handle, so I'll transfer you to the right person.
polite escalation
아, 그건 누나가 알아. 연결해 줄게.
Oh, my sister knows that. I'll put her on.
casual, handing over the phone
nuance: The phrase agents use to transfer your call to another line or department. 연결하다 = 'to connect/link'; 해 드릴게요 makes it a humble promise to do it for you. You'll hear 연결해 드리겠습니다 in the most formal call centers, while 연결해 줄게 works casually when you're just handing your phone to someone nearby.
mistakes: Saying 연결시켜 드릴게요 — the unnecessary causative 시키다 is over-used here; plain 연결해 is cleaner.
Confusing 연결 (connect a call) with 연락 (contact/get in touch) — different actions.

english: They're not available / not in (missed call)
usage: fixed noun — what shows on your screen
examples: 부장님 지금 부재중이세요. 메모 남겨 드릴까요?
The manager is out right now. Shall I take a message?
office phone
부재중 전화가 세 통이나 와 있네.
Whoa, I've got three missed calls.
checking your phone
고객님, 담당자가 부재중입니다. 잠시 후 다시 연락드리겠습니다.
Sir/Ma'am, the agent is unavailable. We'll contact you again shortly.
formal service
nuance: A slightly formal word meaning 'absent / away from one's seat,' used both to explain that someone can't come to the phone and as the label 부재중 전화 for a missed call on your screen. 부재(不在) is Sino-Korean for 'not present,' so it sounds more official than the everyday 없어요. You'll see and hear it constantly in offices and on phones.
mistakes: Pronouncing it 부제중 — it's 부재중 (재, not 제).
Using it for a friend who just stepped out; 잠깐 나갔어요 is more natural casually.

english: I'll get in touch with you later
usage: I'll reach out in a bit
I will get back to you
examples: 지금 좀 바빠서요. 나중에 연락드릴게요.
I'm a bit busy right now. I'll contact you later.
politely ending a call
확인하고 나중에 연락드릴게요.
I'll check and get back to you later.
deferring a decision politely
나 지금 운전 중이야. 나중에 연락할게.
I'm driving right now. I'll call you later.
casual, to a friend
nuance: The polite way to wrap up or postpone contact — you're promising to reach out again. 연락드리다 uses the humble 드리다 ('do for you'), so it raises the listener; with friends it drops to 연락할게. Note it covers both calling and texting, since 연락 means 'contact' in general, not specifically a phone call.
mistakes: Saying 연락드릴게요 to someone clearly below you in status — plain 연락할게요 fits better there.
Mixing up 연락 (contact) with 연결 (connect a call) — they are not interchangeable.

english: I'll put them on / pass you over (to another person)
usage: I'll put them on the line
handing the call to the right person — humble
One moment, I'll pass you over
I'll put the person in charge on
examples: 아, 사장님 찾으세요? 잠시만요, 바꿔 드릴게요.
Oh, you're looking for the boss? One moment, I'll put them on.
office phone hand-off
제가 잘 몰라서요. 아는 사람으로 바꿔 드릴게요.
I'm not sure about this, so I'll put on someone who knows.
polite hand-off
엄마 찾아? 잠깐만, 바꿔 줄게.
Looking for Mom? Hold on, I'll put her on.
casual, at home
nuance: Used when the person who answered hands the phone to whoever the caller actually wants. 바꾸다 literally means 'to change/swap,' and on the phone it means 'swap who's speaking.' This is the household/peer-level counterpart to 연결해 드릴게요: 바꿔 is for handing the same phone over, while 연결 is a technical call transfer.
mistakes: Using 연결해 드릴게요 at home when you're just handing the phone to a family member — 바꿔 드릴게요 is natural.
Writing 바꿔 as 바껴; the stem is 바꾸- (바꾸 + 어 = 바꿔).

usage: I think you have the wrong number
There's no one by that name here
반말 — see note on who's speaking
examples: 김철수요? 전화 잘못 거셨어요. 그런 사람 없는데요.
Kim Chul-su? You've got the wrong number — no one by that name here.
answering a misdial
죄송하지만 전화 잘못 거신 것 같은데요.
Sorry, but I think you've dialed the wrong number.
softened, polite
어? 미안, 내가 전화 잘못 걸었어.
Huh? Sorry, I dialed the wrong number.
the caller admitting their own mistake
nuance: What you say when someone reaches you by mistake — 거셨어요 is the honorific past of 걸다 ('to make a call'), so you're politely telling the caller they dialed wrong. Flip the subject and the caller says 제가 잘못 걸었어요 ('I misdialed'). 걸다 is the standard verb for placing a call (전화를 걸다).
mistakes: Saying 전화 잘못 걸으셨어요 — 걸다 is a ㄹ-irregular: honorific is 거셨어요, not 걸으셨어요.
Using 거셨어요 about yourself; when YOU misdial, say 제가 잘못 걸었어요.

english: Please call back in a little while
usage: asking the caller to retry later
Call back in a bit, please
examples: 지금 회의 중이라, 잠시 후에 다시 걸어 주세요.
I'm in a meeting now, so please call back in a little while.
polite deferral
통화량이 많습니다. 잠시 후에 다시 걸어 주세요.
Call volume is high. Please call again shortly.
automated call-center message
나 밥 먹고 있어. 이따 다시 걸어.
I'm eating. Call me back later.
casual, to a friend
nuance: A polite way to ask the caller to try again soon rather than waiting on the line. 잠시 후에 = 'after a short while,' and 다시 걸어 주세요 ('please dial again') uses the favor verb 주세요. You'll hear the exact phrase in automated messages when lines are busy, so it doubles as a recognizable system prompt.
mistakes: Saying 다시 걸려 주세요 — the active verb is 걸다 (걸어), not the passive 걸리다.
Confusing 잠시 후에 (after a moment) with 잠시만요 (hold on a sec) — different functions.

english: The signal is weak / poor reception
usage: It's because reception is weak here
-아서 giving the reason a call cut out
I can't get a good signal
examples: 여보세요? 여기 신호가 약해서 잘 안 들려요.
Hello? Reception's weak here so I can't hear well.
mid-call connection trouble
지하라서 신호가 약해요. 끊고 다시 걸게요.
I'm underground so the signal's weak. Let me hang up and call back.
explaining and proposing a fix
산속이라 신호 약해. 이따 통화하자.
I'm in the mountains, signal's weak. Let's talk later.
casual
nuance: The natural way to explain why a call sounds bad or keeps dropping — the cellular 신호 ('signal') is 약하다 ('weak'). Koreans also say 신호가 잘 안 잡혀요 ('the signal doesn't get picked up well') for the same idea. Pair it with 잘 안 들려요 to explain that poor reception is why you can't hear.
mistakes: Using 사인(sign) for signal — the cell-reception word is 신호.
Saying 신호가 작아요 (small) — strength is 약하다/세다 (weak/strong), not 작다/크다.

usage: Can you hear me all right?
checking the other side mid-call — honorific
Can you hear my voice clearly?
제 목소리 spells out what they should hear
examples: 여보세요? 제 목소리 잘 들리세요?
Hello? Can you hear my voice okay?
opening check when audio is shaky
여기로 옮겼는데 지금은 잘 들리세요?
I moved over here — is it clear now?
confirming after relocating
야, 잘 들려? 자꾸 끊기는 것 같은데.
Hey, can you hear me? It keeps cutting out.
casual
nuance: The flip side of 잘 안 들려요 — instead of reporting your own trouble, you ask whether the other person can hear you. 들리다 is the intransitive 'to be heard,' and the honorific 들리세요? politely asks about their experience. It's the go-to reception check on calls and video meetings alike.
mistakes: Saying 잘 듣고 있어요? (are you listening?) when you mean 'can you hear me' — use 들리세요?, not 듣다.
Confusing 들리다 (be audible) with 들다 (lift/hold) — different verbs entirely.

english: They're on another call right now
usage: They're on the phone right now
The line's busy / on a call
I'm on the phone right now
examples: 부장님 지금 통화 중이세요. 잠시 후에 다시 걸어 주세요.
The manager's on another call. Please call back shortly.
office phone
몇 번을 걸어도 계속 통화 중이네요.
No matter how many times I call, the line's still busy.
frustrated caller
미안, 나 지금 통화 중이야. 이따 연락할게.
Sorry, I'm on the phone. I'll get back to you.
casual, about yourself
nuance: Explains that someone's line is occupied — 통화 중 literally means 'in the middle of a call.' Add the honorific -세요 when it's about a person you respect (지금 통화 중이세요), but use plain 통화 중이에요 about a line or yourself. Distinct from 부재중이에요 (away from the phone): 통화 중 means they're there but already talking.
mistakes: Mixing up 통화 중 (on a call) with 부재중 (away/absent) — opposite situations.
Adding -세요 when talking about your own call; for yourself say 통화 중이에요/통화 중이야.
